decision: ACCEPT Peerit release sequence 25 as the LIVE bounded-public-test launch successor: the first-visit seed-recovery liveness fix — the cold head-to-genesis descriptor chain-walk and the seed Cell-GET fallback now retry ONLY transient transport failures (bounded, with backoff), so a single sub-second network abort no longer flips a fresh first visit to blocked-seed-recovery — keeping the limited Cell-GET runtime authority EXPOSED at sequence 25 and signed seed recovery ENABLED for the same 34-record live launch seed. The exact production CSP remains unchanged, authenticated browser authority MUST become active before any relay I/O, recovery performs zero network PUTs, ordinary delivery remains LOCAL_ONLY, the all-five successor remains excluded, and the GA product gate remains blocked with all 22 blockers disclosed-open.

authority.owner_instruction: Live first-visit seed recovery on peerit.site (seq-24 deployed) intermittently blocks at blocked-seed-recovery. Reproduced against the live relays with a first-visit soak harness (fresh browser context per boot, no persisted floor): a SINGLE sub-second transient transport abort (TypeError Failed to fetch / TRANSPORT_FAILURE) landing anywhere in the zero-retry, SEQUENTIAL head-to-genesis descriptor describe-walk fails the whole relay qualification and blocks recovery; a transient burst spanning both replicas of one record likewise exhausts Cell-GET fallback. No timeout ever fires naturally — this is a liveness/robustness defect, not a deadline tuning issue. Make the first-visit walk and the Cell-GET fallback retry transient transport failures ONLY, bounded with backoff, keeping every signature/chain-continuity/admission/epoch-window check exactly as strict.

root_cause.mechanism: first-visit (cold, no persisted discovery floor) seed recovery re-walks each relay's signed descriptor chain head-to-genesis with one sequential describe round-trip per link (syd-1 now 23 links, dal-1 now 20 links to pinned genesis) and then reads the 39 launch cells. The walk carries no overall deadline and had NO retry, so a single transient transport abort (a dropped connection / network change / the vendored client's own per-request deadline truncating one response) threw TRANSPORT_FAILURE and failed the entire relay qualification, surfacing as blocked-seed-recovery. A transient burst aborting both replicas of one record inside a single fallback pass likewise produced PEERIT_COLD_READER_RECORD_UNAVAILABLE. Reproduction: 4/10 baseline boots and up to 4/10 slow-link boots blocked; every natural abort was a sub-second transport event, never a deadline. Two further transient classes surfaced across the soak, dominated by the relay blind-edge degradation window of 2026-08-05 19:00-21:00 UTC: a TRUNCATED HTTP body — the relay edge closing the connection mid-response so the vendored client reads fewer bytes than the declared size class — surfacing as RELAY_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION "bootstrap response is shorter than the selected class" on the describe walk and "response is shorter than the selected class" on the health-challenge / Cell-GET reads (the incomplete body is never parsed, verified, or accepted, so re-asking relaxes nothing); and a sustained natural burst that exhausted the original short retry window. Every observed block was a transient short read or transport event, never a deadline firing and never a verification failure.
liveness_fix_applied: js/substrate/relay-consumer.js qualifyLimitedSeedRelay: every relay fetch in the qualification — fetchDescriptorHead, fetchDescriptorHistory (the head-to-genesis chain-walk), AND qualifyCellGetCandidate (the DESCRIBE.CHALLENGE health proof over the direct client) — is now wrapped in fetchDescriptorWithTransientRetry: a bounded (6 attempts, exponential backoff 400ms x 2^attempt → a ~12s cumulative window, abortable) retry of ONLY transient transport failures (error.code TRANSPORT_FAILURE, error.name AbortError, or a fetch TypeError). Verification errors (chain discontinuity, duplicate, genesis mismatch, admission drift, bad signature, not-qualified / health rejection) are never retried and still fail closed immediately; an explicit caller/lifecycle abort is never retried.

js/substrate/cold-reader.mjs seed cold reader: the per-record replica fallback now runs a bounded number of extra passes (up to 3, 400ms backoff, abortable) ONLY when every replica failure in a pass was a transient transport abort; a verification failure breaks immediately. Fallback order and the runtime-gate forced-fault accounting (networkGets 40, fallbackCount 1, syd 1) are preserved.

Both classifiers additionally retry the exact vendored truncated-body short-read messages under the SAME bounded budget: js/substrate/relay-consumer.js isTransientDescriptorFetchFailure accepts RELAY_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION "bootstrap response is shorter than the selected class" AND "response is shorter than the selected class" (the describe/bootstrap reader and the health-challenge/generic reader each emit their own variant mid-walk), and js/substrate/cold-reader.mjs isTransientCellGetFailure accepts RELAY_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION "response is shorter than the selected class". A truncated body is never parsed, verified, or accepted, so re-asking relaxes nothing; every OTHER RELAY_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (framing, wrong content-length, trailing bytes, malformed frame, or a near-miss rewording) still fails closed forever. test/peerit-transient-fetch-classifiers.mjs pins the exact message scope and the verbatim vendored strings.
root_cause.no_weakening: descriptor signature, chain continuity to pinned genesis, hash, epoch-window, admission-parameter signature + window verification, and the descriptor-driven admission binding are all unchanged. Retry applies ONLY to the network fetch of a descriptor or cell — every fetched value still passes the exact same verification before acceptance; a verification failure is never retried and still fails closed. The only change is that a transient transport abort is retried instead of instantly failing the whole cold walk.
